why: Swaps build-then-reveal for reveal-then-build. Both statements still run, so a test that only counts worlds and seeds cannot see it -- what changes is that `enterGameplay` is handed the STALE `currentSession`, the one resolved against the world the player abandoned, and the state change that hides the application ground reaches the screen before the landing board exists. The visible half is a frame of the abandoned board; the recorded half is a resolved session that does not describe the world underneath it. Ordering is the property the comment at this site claims, so it gets an entry rather than a promise.
